html:
Andronikos I Komnenos was Byzantine emperor from 1183 to 1185, the last ruler of the Komnenos dynasty. A grandson of Alexios I, he was handsome, clever and reckless, and spent much of the reign of his cousin Manuel I in plots, escapes, prisons and scandalous love affairs, from Kiev to Jerusalem.

After Manuel died in 1180, the regency for the boy Alexios II was led by his mother, the Latin princess Maria of Antioch, and was seen as favouring Italian merchants. In 1182 Andronikos marched on Constantinople with popular support, and his arrival set off the Massacre of the Latins. He had the empress-mother and then the young emperor killed, made himself emperor, and married Alexios's twelve-year-old widow.

He attacked corruption and the abuses of great landowners, but with growing terror against anyone he suspected. In 1185 the Normans of Sicily invaded and took Thessalonica in the sack of Thessalonica. Panic in the capital raised Isaac Angelos to the throne. Andronikos was caught, tortured and handed to the mob, which killed him in the Hippodrome.
